relationships.description: Apple Inc.'s effective tax rate for the first quarter of 2026 was lower than the statutory federal income tax rate.
Foreign currency loss regulations were issued by the U.S. Department of Treasury in December 2024.
Tax impact from foreign currency revaluations in the first quarter of 2025 related to the State Aid Decision.
Apple Inc. utilizes several outsourcing partners to manufacture subassemblies for its products.
Apple Inc. performs final assembly of finished products.
Apple Inc. performs testing of finished products.
Apple Inc. obtains individual components for its products from a wide variety of individual suppliers.
Apple Inc. had manufacturing purchase obligations of $44.4B as of December 27, 2025.
Apple Inc. had other purchase obligations of $35.1B as of December 27, 2025.
Apple Inc. has an authorized share repurchase program.
Apple Inc. repurchased $25.0B of its common stock during the first quarter of 2026.
Apple Inc. paid dividends and dividend equivalents of $3.9B during the first quarter of 2026.
Apple Inc. intends to increase its dividend on an annual basis, subject to declaration by the Board of Directors.
The Board of Directors declares the dividend.
In September 2025, the Financial Accounting Standards Board issued ASU 2025-06.
ASU 2025-06 removes all references to software development stages.
ASU 2025-06 requires capitalization of software costs when management has committed to the software project and it is probable the software will be completed and perform its intended use.
ASU 2025-06 will be effective for Apple Inc. in its first quarter of 2029.
Apple Inc. is currently evaluating the timing and method of its adoption of ASU 2025-06.
In November 2024, the FASB issued ASU 2024-03.
In January 2025, the FASB issued ASU 2025-01 clarifying the effective date of ASU 2024-03.
ASU 2024-03 will require Apple Inc. to disclose amounts of purchases of inventory, employee compensation, depreciation, and intangible asset amortization.
Apple Inc. will adopt ASU 2024-03 in its fourth quarter of 2028 using a prospective transition method.
In December 2023, the FASB issued ASU 2023-09.
